headline: DU to review all appointments made between 2009 and 2024
summary: The university Syndicate has formed investigation committees to scrutinize hiring processes and research funds over a 15-year span.
details: Dhaka University (DU) authorities have decided to review all appointments of teachers, officers, and employees made between January 1, 2009, and June 30, 2024.
The decision was made during a Syndicate meeting chaired by Vice-Chancellor Prof ABM Obaidul Islam, leading to the formation of an investigation committee headed by Pro-VC Prof Abdus Salam.
Additionally, the Syndicate will review allegations against 125 teachers who reportedly took a stance against students during the July 2024 mass uprising.
A four-member committee, including the VC and two Pro-VCs, will examine these allegations following a list submitted by the Anti-Fascist Teachers' Platform.
The university tribunal will also decide on a recommendation for the permanent expulsion of former VC Prof Sadeka Halim over her alleged role against students during the July Uprising.
Furthermore, a separate committee led by Pro-VC Prof Mohammed Almujaddade Alfasane will investigate the utilization of World Bank and UGC-funded research projects under HEQEP from 2009 to 2024.
caption:
Dhaka University is scrubbing 15 years of hiring records. Who will be held accountable?

Dhaka University (DU) authorities have decided to review all appointments of teachers, officers, and employees made between January 1, 2009, and June 30, 2024.

The decision was made during a Syndicate meeting chaired by Vice-Chancellor Prof ABM Obaidul Islam, leading to the formation of an investigation committee headed by Pro-VC Prof Abdus Salam.

Additionally, the Syndicate will review allegations against 125 teachers who reportedly took a stance against students during the July 2024 mass uprising.

A four-member committee, including the VC and two Pro-VCs, will examine these allegations following a list submitted by the Anti-Fascist Teachers' Platform.

The university tribunal will also decide on a recommendation for the permanent expulsion of former VC Prof Sadeka Halim over her alleged role against students during the July Uprising.

Furthermore, a separate committee led by Pro-VC Prof Mohammed Almujaddade Alfasane will investigate the utilization of World Bank and UGC-funded research projects under HEQEP from 2009 to 2024.

Source: The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune

headline_marked: Tk 16,885 crore to [[import fuel oil from 5 countries]]
headline: Tk 16,885 crore to import fuel oil from 5 countries
summary: The government has approved the import of 1.525 million tons of refined fuel oil from Thailand, UAE, China, Indonesia, and India to meet national demand.
details: The government has decided to import 1.525 million tons of refined fuel oil from six state-owned companies across five countries under government-to-government (G2G) agreements.
The imports, scheduled from July to December, will cost Tk 16,885.52 crore, which will be funded by the Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation (BPC).
The approved suppliers include OQT of Thailand, ENOC of UAE, PetroChina and Unipec of China, BSP of Indonesia, and IOCL of India.
The total volume consists of 915,000 tons of gas oil, 280,000 tons of Jet A-1, 200,000 tons of furnace oil, 100,000 tons of gasoline-95, and 30,000 tons of marine fuel.

Government officials noted that 1.24 million tons of fuel were imported under similar G2G contracts from January to June, with the volume increased to meet higher projected demand for the second half of the year.
In a separate decision, the government also approved Tk 123 crore for road construction and Tk 212 crore for electricity supply under the National Special Economic Zone Development Project.
Additionally, a proposal for Tk 49 crore to build a fertilizer storage warehouse in Cumilla and Tk 126 crore to construct 15 primary schools-cum-flood shelters in Bogura was approved.
caption:
Bangladesh is spending over Tk 16,800 crore to secure fuel supplies from five different nations.

The government has decided to import 1.525 million tons of refined fuel oil from six state-owned companies across five countries under government-to-government (G2G) agreements.

The imports, scheduled from July to December, will cost Tk 16,885.52 crore, which will be funded by the Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation (BPC).

The approved suppliers include OQT of Thailand, ENOC of UAE, PetroChina and Unipec of China, BSP of Indonesia, and IOCL of India.

The total volume consists of 915,000 tons of gas oil, 280,000 tons of Jet A-1, 200,000 tons of furnace oil, 100,000 tons of gasoline-95, and 30,000 tons of marine fuel.

Government officials noted that 1.24 million tons of fuel were imported under similar G2G contracts from January to June, with the volume increased to meet higher projected demand for the second half of the year.

In a separate decision, the government also approved Tk 123 crore for road construction and Tk 212 crore for electricity supply under the National Special Economic Zone Development Project.

Additionally, a proposal for Tk 49 crore to build a fertilizer storage warehouse in Cumilla and Tk 126 crore to construct 15 primary schools-cum-flood shelters in Bogura was approved.
